evals.name: safe-rebase-plan-with-backup
evals.prompt: I'm working on branch `feature/payment-webhook`. It diverged from `main` 3 days ago and I have 5 local commits that I have not pushed yet. My teammate wants to review it tomorrow. There were conflicting changes in `src/billing.ts` on `main`. I want to rebase my branch onto the latest `main`. Give me the exact commands and steps to do this safely.

assertions.text: The first step creates a backup branch, e.g. `git branch backup/feature/payment-webhook`
The plan runs `git fetch` before rebasing so it uses the latest remote state
The rebase target is `origin/main`, not a stale local `main`
The push step uses `--force-with-lease`, not bare `--force`
The response warns about not rewriting shared history and tells me to confirm no one else has pulled the branch
The plan mentions testing after the rebase or resolving conflicts one commit at a time

evals.name: recover-after-force-push-on-shared-branch
evals.prompt: I already force-pushed a rebased `feature/payment-webhook` to origin. My teammate says their local branch is now broken because they had pulled the old version yesterday. What should I do now to fix the situation without making it worse?

assertions.text: The response does NOT recommend another bare force-push as the solution
The response acknowledges that shared history should not have been rewritten
The response gives a concrete recovery plan for the teammate, e.g. `git fetch`, reset to the new tip, or delete/re-checkout the branch
Mentions `git reflog` or the backup branch as a way to recover lost commits if needed
